16567-aunt-jane-s-nieces-in-the-red-cros.title: Aunt Jane'S Nieces In The Red Cross
16567-aunt-jane-s-nieces-in-the-red-cros.creator: Edith Van Dyne
16567-aunt-jane-s-nieces-in-the-red-cros.description: A book by Edith Van Dyne. Hers was a dark olive complexion, face of exquisite contour, great brown eyes with a wealth of hair to match them and the flush of a rose in her rounded cheeks. The poise of her girlish figure was gracious and dignified as the bearing of a queen.

32990-a-day-with-lord-byron.title: A Day With Lord Byron
32990-a-day-with-lord-byron.creator: Unknown
32990-a-day-with-lord-byron.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. There's not a joy the world can give like that it takes away,   When the glow of early thought declines in feeling's dull decay;   'Tis not on youth's smooth cheek the blush alone, which fades so fast,   But the tender bloom of heart is gone, ere youth itself be past.

arxiv-2401-18031.title: A note on the density of periodic orbits of Anosov geodesic flow in manifolds of finite volume
arxiv-2401-18031.creator: Nestor Nina Zarate, Sergio Romaña
arxiv-2401-18031.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nestor Nina Zarate, Sergio Romaña. In this paper, we prove that manifolds of finite volume with Anosov geodesic flow have dense periodic orbits. The same result works for conservative Anosov flows in non-compact cases. Keywords: Geodesic Flow, Shadowing Lemma, Stable(Unstable) Manifolds. Presentation:
This article was organized by Sergio Romaña as a tribute to the author Nestor Nina Zarate, a young Bolivian mathematician, with training in Bolivia and Brazil, who left us too soon, but who left us with his valuable contribution to mathematical sciences.

arxiv-2409-02645.title: Emergent Language: A Survey and Taxonomy
arxiv-2409-02645.creator: Jannik Peters, Constantin Waubert de Puiseau, Hasan Tercan, Arya Gopikrishnan, Gustavo Adolpho Lucas De Carvalho, Christian Bitter, Tobias Meisen
arxiv-2409-02645.description: Abstract The field of emergent language represents a novel area of research within the domain of artificial intelligence, particularly within the context of multi-agent reinforcement learning. Although the concept of studying language emergence is not new, early approaches were primarily concerned with explaining human language formation, with little consideration given to its potential utility for artificial agents.

arxiv-2410-09952.title: large scale longitudinal experiments: estimation and Inference
arxiv-2410-09952.creator: Apoorva Lal, Alex Fischer, Matthew Wardrop
arxiv-2410-09952.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Apoorva Lal, Alex Fischer, Matthew Wardrop. Large-scale randomized experiments are seldom analyzed using panel regression methods because of computational challenges arising from the presence of millions of nuisance parameters. We leverage \textcite mundlak1978pooling’s insight that unit intercepts can be eliminated by using carefully chosen averages of the regressors to rewrite several common estimators in a form that is amenable to weighted-least squares estimation with frequency weights.

arxiv-2503-05720.title: That is Unacceptable: the Moral Foundations of Canceling
arxiv-2503-05720.creator: Soda Marem Lo, Oscar Araque, Rajesh Sharma, Marco Antonio Stranisci
arxiv-2503-05720.description: Abstract Canceling is a morally-driven phenomenon that hinders the development of safe social media platforms and contributes to ideological polarization. To address this issue we present the C anceling A ttitudes De ection (CADE) dataset, an annotated corpus of canceling incidents aimed at exploring the factors of disagreements in evaluating people canceling attitudes on social media.

arxiv-2505-13273.title: Seeing the Unseen: How EMoE Unveils Bias in Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
arxiv-2505-13273.creator: Lucas Berry Axel Brando Wei-Di Chang, Juan Camilo Gamboa Higuera David Meger
arxiv-2505-13273.description: Abstract Estimating uncertainty in text-to-image diffusion models is challenging because of their large parameter counts (often exceeding 100 million) and operation in complex, high-dimensional spaces with virtually infinite input possibilities. In this paper, we propose Epistemic Mixture of Experts (EMoE), a novel framework for efficiently estimating epistemic uncertainty in diffusion models.

arxiv-2506-11320.title: Suppressing spurious oscillations and particle noise in particle-in-cell simulations
arxiv-2506-11320.creator: Yuxi Chen, Hongyang Zhou, Gábor Tóth
arxiv-2506-11320.description: Abstract Particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations are essential for studying kinetic plasma processes, but they often suffer from statistical noise, especially in plasmas with fast flows. We have also found that the typical central difference scheme used in PIC codes to solve Maxwell’s equations produces spurious oscillations near discontinuities, which can lead to unphysical solutions.

The Transforming Growth Factor (TGF) β signalling family includes morphogens, such as Nodal and Activin, with important functions in vertebrate development. pmc-11283789.title: Comparative Analysis of Logistic Regression, Gradient Boosted Trees, SVM, and Random Forest Algorithms for Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury Requiring Dialysis After Cardiac Surgery
pmc-11283789.creator: Evi Diana Omar, Hasnah Mat, Ainil Zafirah Abd Karim, Ridwan Sanaudi, Fairol H Ibrahim, Mohd Azahadi Omar, Muhd Zulfadli Hafiz Ismail, Vivek Jason Jayaraj, Bak Leong Goh
pmc-11283789.description: PurposeThis study aimed to identify the best-performing algorithm for predicting Acute Kidney Injury (AKI) necessitating dialysis following cardiac surgery.Patients and MethodsThe dataset encompassed patient data from a tertiary cardiothoracic center in Malaysia between 2011 and 2015, sourced from electronic health records. Extensive preprocessing and feature selection ensured data quality and relevance.

pmc-11506556.title: TRPV4 Mediates Alveolar Epithelial Barrier Integrity and Induces ADAM10-Driven E-Cadherin Shedding
pmc-11506556.creator: Lena Schaller, Thomas Gudermann, Alexander Dietrich, Konstantin G Birukov
pmc-11506556.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) channels have been associated with numerous pulmonary pathologies, including hypertension, asthma, and acute lung injury. However, their role in the alveolar epithelium remains unclear. We performed impedance-based resistance measurements in primary differentiated alveolar epithelial type I (AT1) cells from wild-type (WT) and TRPV4-deficient (TRPV4−/−) C57/BL6J mice to detect changes in AT1 barrier integrity upon TRPV4 activation.

pmc-11604317.title: Food choice, embodied knowledge and circumscribed agency: factors influencing adolescent girls’ and boys’ dietary practices in three states in northern Nigeria
pmc-11604317.creator: Abigail Conrad, Akriti Singh, Sharmila Mysore, Stanley Nwosu, Michael Daniel Eveshoyan, Usman Ibraheem
pmc-11604317.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Objective:The objective of this study was to explore adolescent dietary practices, related norms and acceptable communication platforms in northern Nigeria to inform future nutrition project design.Design:This was a qualitative formative research study. We used purposive sampling and conducted thirty focus group discussions with male and female adolescents aged 10–14 and 15–19 years (n 180) and six with adult influencers (n 36).

pmc-12546717.title: The RESILIENT Dataset: Multimodal Monitoring of Ageing-Related Comorbidities and Cognitive Decline
pmc-12546717.creator: Nathalia Céspedes Gómez, Yu Chen, Samaneh Kouchaki, Mahan Heydari, Alexandra Cairns, Sergio David Sierra Marín, Alexander Capstick, Jaye Somers, Kirsty Harris, Wilson Wen Bin Goh, Chloe Walsh, Jessica True, Olga Balazikova, Ramin Nilforooshan, Payam Barnaghi
pmc-12546717.description: The growing ageing population and prevalence of comorbidities pose significant healthcare challenges, from increasing hospitalisations to dementia risk. Healthcare systems primarily treat single conditions, overlooking the complex interplay of chronic diseases. Advances in wearable technology and remote healthcare monitoring technologies offer opportunities to enhance management of comorbidities and early intervention to improve healthcare outcomes.

pmc-12768654.title: PP10 Automated Calculation Of Absolute Effects Using The Abseff Program: A Descriptive Study
pmc-12768654.creator: Carolina Latorraca, Rafael Leite Pacheco, Patricia Parreira, Ana Luiza Cabrera Martimbianco, Verônica Colpani, Isabela Porto de Toledo, Roberta Borges Silva, Camila Monteiro Cruz, Cecília Menezes Farinasso, Rachel Riera
pmc-12768654.description: IntroductionOne way of communicating the effect of interventions is by converting relative effects, such as relative risk, into absolute effects. Guidelines from the GRADE working group and the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions recommend this conversion for summarizing and concluding evidence syntheses.

pmc-12831352.title: Trimester-specific association of maternal prenatal physical activities with risk of preterm birth: a prospective pre-birth cohort study
pmc-12831352.creator: Jiajin Hu, Yanan Ma, Wenhan Jia, Ningyu Wan, Xiaochuan Wang, Lu Zheng, Zhe Yang, Dongming Zheng, Jun Wei, Deliang Wen
pmc-12831352.description: This study aimed to examine the trimester-specific association of maternal prenatal physical activities (PA) with risk of preterm birth (PTB). We recruited 2080 women during the first trimester and conducted follow-ups during the second and third trimesters and at birth.

pmc-13115851.title: Determinants of Chemotherapy Convenience and Satisfaction: The Role of Symptom and Psychological Burden in Cancer Patients—A Cross-Sectional Study
pmc-13115851.creator: Evangelos C. Fradelos, Konstantinos Skampardonis, Pavlos Sarafis, Alexios Alexopoulos, Aikaterini Toska, Maria Saridi, Theocharis I. Konstantinidis, Maria Lavdaniti, Paul Cella, Athanasios Kotsakis, Filippos Koinis
pmc-13115851.description: Background: Chemotherapy-related symptom burden and psychological distress may significantly influence patients’ perceptions of treatment convenience and satisfaction, yet evidence in the Greek oncology population remains limited. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted among 150 cancer patients receiving chemotherapy in a tertiary hospital. Data were collected using CCSQ, ESAS-r, PHQ-2, GAD-2, and WHO-5.

pmc-13279694.title: Biomechanical finite element methods study of a novel internal fixation system for lumbar spondylolysis
pmc-13279694.creator: Jingyuan Li, ChengFei Du, Yulei Wang, Di Du, Jinlong Liang, Nengqi Shao, Fanzhe Feng, Wenhao Xu, Yongqing Xu, Yi Cui
pmc-13279694.description: ObjectivesThis study aimed to evaluate the biomechanical efficacy of a novel internal fixation system for the treatment of lumbar spondylolysis (LS). In addition, the changes in the mechanical performance of the proposed fixation construct during progressive compression were systematically investigated.

pmc-13300873.title: Predicting atrial fibrillation in heart failure: added value of a plasma protein risk score over clinical and genomic models
pmc-13300873.creator: M T Huttelmaier, S Zeid, A Gieswinkel, T Koeck, V Ten Cate, S Stoerk, S Frantz, P Lurz, T Fischer, P Wild
pmc-13300873.description: IntroductionAtrial fibrillation (AF) commonly coexists with heart failure (HF), aggravating disease progression and prognosis. Early diagnosis and treatment of AF in heart failure (HF) is crucial as the two conditions mutually reinforce each other resulting in adverse outcome and prognosis.

pmc-13424553.title: Machine-learned global glacier ice volumes
pmc-13424553.creator: Niccolò Maffezzoli, Eric Rignot, Carlo Barbante, Mathieu Morlighem, Troels C Petersen, Sebastiano Vascon
pmc-13424553.description: We present a global dataset of glacier ice thickness modeled with IceBoost v2.0, a gradient-boosted decision tree scheme trained on 7 million ice thickness measurements and informed by physical and geometrical predictors. We model the distributed ice thickness for every glacier in the two latest Randolph Glacier Inventory releases (RGI v6.0 and v7.

pmc-13459276.title: Use of contrast-enhanced mammography for preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion status in invasive breast cancer
pmc-13459276.creator: Liya Gong, Muzi Wen, Ying Ye, Zhiyue Zhao, Junyan Wen, Ziqi Wu, Yanyu Hao, Xiaomei Huang
pmc-13459276.description: BackgroundTo investigate the use of contrast-enhanced mammography (CEM) for preoperative prediction of lymphovascular invasion (LVI) status in invasive breast cancer.MethodsA total of 243 female patients diagnosed with invasive breast cancer (median age: 49 years; range: 27–77 years) who received preoperative CEM examination in our hospital between September 2018 and February 2024 were retrospectively collected and analyzed.

pmc-13521755.title: Results of the 2025 Training Program for Healthcare Workers in Emerging and Bioterrorism-related Infectious Disease Response
pmc-13521755.creator: Eunsil Kim, Eun-Mi Park, Young-Man Kim, Bryan Inho Kim, Yu-Jeong Min, 은실 김, 은미 박, 영만 김, 인호 김, 유정 민
pmc-13521755.description: ObjectivesThe 2025 training program for healthcare workers in emerging and bioterrorism-related infectious disease response was conducted to develop professionals capable of responding rapidly to outbreaks. This study analyzed the program’s results, evaluated its effectiveness, and proposed future directions for improvement.MethodsThe curriculum comprised 14 sessions divided into three basic and four advanced courses.

pmc-13526347.title: Efficacy of Pulsed Radiofrequency Combination Therapy for Postherpetic Neuralgia: A Systematic Review and Bayesian Network Meta-Analysis
pmc-13526347.creator: Beibei Li, Xiong Xiang, Ranyu Li, Peng Zhou, Jian Jia
pmc-13526347.description: BackgroundPostherpetic neuralgia (PHN) lowers quality of life. However, the comparative efficacy of pulsed radiofrequency (PRF)-based combination therapies remains unclear. This study compared different PRF combination regimens for PHN.MethodsEight databases were searched up to July 25, 2025. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 and the Newcastle‑Ottawa Scale.

pmc-13608034.title: Epidemiology, Clinicopathological Features, Etiological Spectrum and Outcomes of Subcutaneous Mycoses: A 14-Year Retrospective Study
pmc-13608034.creator: Qiannan Jia, Aiping Fan, Xiuli Xie, Jun Li, Li Zhang, Qiwen Yang
pmc-13608034.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Subcutaneous mycoses are a group of chronic deep fungal infections involving the skin and subcutaneous tissue. In this study, we characterized their epidemiology, diagnostic findings, treatment, and outcomes in a referral cohort from Beijing, China. Methods: We retrospectively reviewed 86 patients diagnosed with subcutaneous mycoses at a referral center in Beijing which serves a notable population from northeastern agricultural regions, from 2012 to 2025.
